armed.text: A vending machine stands against the wall, glass intact, every coil empty but one. Bottom row, far left: a single can, red and silver. The glass is the toughened kind, so the only way to it is an arm up through the delivery flap, and somebody has wired the flap. Jump leads run from it to a car battery on the floor, an ignition coil taped on top and a little black box that clicks once a second, like it is counting. Beside the flap, eleven fingertip scorch marks, each one circled and dated.

choices.label: Leave the can and back out the way you came
Find the battery terminal and pull the lead

escaped.text: You back away from the machine the way you would back away from a dog, and the clicking follows you as far as the door. Eleven scorch marks, circled and dated. You decline to be twelve. Behind you the can sits in its coil, the last of its kind, guarded by a car battery with a grudge.

cache_1.text: You get your sleeve over your hand and pull the lead off the terminal, and the clicking stops mid-count. Then you put your arm up through the flap to the shoulder, which takes more nerve than anything you have done all week, and close your fingers on the can. Warm, dented, sealed. The label says {{drink}}. You coil the jump leads while you are down there. Somebody up there has a sense of humour.

choices.label: Lever the back panel off and see what else it kept

cache_2.text: The back comes off and the machine's guts are yours: motors, a tangle of good copper, and the coin box, full to the lip. Years of exact change, gone green and fused into a single brick. Every coin anyone ever lost to this thing is in here, and you would bet one of them started all this. You would bet money, if money were worth anything. As of today it is worth {{worth}}.

the_ankle.text: You step on a jump lead on the way out and the clip flips up and bites you through the sock. Your leg performs a short, vigorous dance without consulting you, and you kick the machine hard enough to hurt the machine. Afterwards there is a neat round burn on your ankle the size of a coin. Exact change.

the_flap.text: You reach round the back for the terminal and lean your forearm on the side of the machine, which it turns out is also on the circuit. Every muscle you own agrees to do the same thing at once. Your teeth shut on your tongue. Your hair gets up to look around. Your bladder makes a unilateral decision, and when you come round on the floor the little box is still going, click, click, adding you to the tally.

the_savings.text: The little black box was not just counting. It was saving up. Your pry bar finds the one screw it is wired to, and everything it has put by since the last visitor arrives in a single white snap. You wake across the room smelling of burnt eyebrow, which is what it is, your fillings humming a note you can feel in your knees. The pry bar stays where it was, welded to the screw.

drink: JOLT COLA — NOW WITH MORE KICK
worth: almost exactly its weight in washers
